scenarios.draft: Test successful update of a member's display_name, profile_image_url, and is_active by an administrator. First, register a new member with valid details using the POST /discussionBoard/actors/members endpoint. Then, as an admin, perform a PUT request to update the member's display_name, assign a new valid profile_image_url, and set is_active to false. Verify the response returns the updated member record and all changes are persisted. Updates to deleted members should be forbidden (see separate scenario).

dependencies.purpose: Register a member whose fields will be edited in this scenario. Required to have a valid member id.

scenarios.draft: Test forbidden update attempt on a soft-deleted member account. Create a new member, then soft-delete the member using DELETE /discussionBoard/actors/members/{id}. Afterwards, try updating display_name or profile_image_url and verify that the operation is rejected with a 404 or forbidden error, confirming business logic denies updates to deleted members.

dependencies.purpose: Register the member account that will be subsequently soft deleted.
Soft delete the registered member so that update operations should be forbidden.

scenarios.draft: Test update attempt on a non-existent member ID. Generate a random UUID that does not correspond to any member in the database. Attempt to update the display_name and verify the system responds with a 404 not found error, demonstrating proper handling of missing members.

Test successful soft deletion of a member account by an administrator. First, create a new member using POST /discussionBoard/actors/members and ensure is_active=true. As an administrator, soft-delete the member and verify that the response confirms success (null response or expected soft delete outcome) and that the member no longer appears in standard member listings.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member whose account will be soft deleted for this test.

scenarios.draft: Test the behavior when attempting to soft delete a member that is already soft deleted. Create a member, perform a soft delete, then attempt to delete the same member again. Confirm that the system responds with either a 404 or an appropriate status indicating the member is already deleted and cannot be soft deleted twice.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member account that will be soft deleted.
First soft delete to prepare for the redundant deletion scenario.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to soft delete a member using a non-existent UUID. Generate a random UUID that does not correspond to any member, perform the DELETE, and confirm the system responds with a not found error (404), ensuring robust handling of deletion requests for absent members.

Test the successful revocation of a moderator assignment by setting the 'revoked_at' field. First, an administrator creates a member, then escalates them to a moderator via the assignment endpoint. Then the moderator's role is revoked using this update endpoint, and the system should reflect that revoked_at is properly set. This checks business workflow for moderator demotion and auditability.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member who can be escalated to moderator.
Assign moderator role to the test member to create a moderator assignment record that can be updated.

scenarios.draft: Validate that attempting to update non-schema fields or violate update rules (for example, trying to set an immutable field like 'id', or trying to update revoked_at to an invalid value) results in a failure. The response should be an error indicating allowed updatable fields and validation constraints.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member to use as the assignment base.
Assign moderator role to enable updating an assignment.

scenarios.draft: Test that attempting to update a moderator assignment record using a non-existent id results in a not-found error. This validates error handling when referencing invalid or deleted assignments.

Test successful deletion (hard delete) of a moderator assignment. First, a member is created and assigned as moderator. The delete operation is then called with the moderator assignment's id. The expected outcome is that the record is fully removed and cannot be retrieved afterward (responds with 404 on get).

dependencies.purpose: Create member to assign as moderator.
Assign moderator role to generate an assignment id for deletion.

scenarios.draft: Test attempting to delete a moderator assignment using a non-existent id, expecting a not-found (404) error. This ensures proper error messaging for invalid deletes.

Verify administrator assignment succeeds when referencing an existing discussion_board_member. First, ensure the member record exists (using the members endpoint), then escalate them to administrator status using this endpoint. The response should include a valid administrator assignment entry reflecting data persistence and schema compliance.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member to be escalated to administrator.

scenarios.draft: Validate that attempting to assign administrator status to a member who is already an administrator returns a uniqueness violation error, enforcing one admin assignment per member at a time.

dependencies.purpose: Create member for admin role assignment.
Assign admin once; second attempt with same member triggers uniqueness constraint.

scenarios.draft: Test failure scenario where administrator assignment is attempted with a non-existent, soft-deleted, or already-revoked member id. The system should reject the request and return a foreign key error or a meaningful invalid assignment error.

Test searching, filtering, and paginating administrator assignments. After creating multiple administrators, query this endpoint using filters such as member_id, assigned_at, revoked_at and pagination parameters. Response should match requested criteria and segregate revoked from active assignments.

dependencies.purpose: Create several members to serve as administrator assignment subjects.
Create multiple administrator assignments for filter and pagination validation.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a paginated list with filters that intentionally produce no matching assignments (e.g., using bogus or date-range criteria). The system should return an empty data array but still provide valid pagination metadata.

Verify successful retrieval of a specific administrator assignment by id. The test should create a member, assign administrator role, then fetch the assignment details using this endpoint, validating correctness of the returned record.

dependencies.purpose: Create member for administrator assignment.
Create the administrator assignment to supply a real id for retrieval.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving administrator assignment detail with a non-existent or deleted id, expecting a 404 not found error. This checks error handling of invalid resource queries.

A member attempts to delete one of their own search history records using its valid UUID. First, a member account must be created and authenticated. Next, the member performs a search, which creates a new search history entry. The test then deletes this search history entry using its UUID. The test verifies that the deletion succeeds and that subsequent attempts to retrieve this record return a not-found error, confirming hard deletion.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new member account to perform search-related actions as an authenticated user.
Create a new search history entry for the member, which will then be targeted for deletion.
Used to (a) ensure the record exists before deletion and (b) verify it returns a not-found error after deletion.

scenarios.draft: Test deletion attempt for a non-existent (random or deleted) search history record by a valid member. After registering and authenticating as a member, the test submits a DELETE request for a search history ID that does not exist in the system. The service must respond with an appropriate not-found error, and no records should be affected in the database.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new member to ensure the deletion request is coming from an authenticated context.

scenarios.draft: A member attempts to delete another member’s search history record. Two member accounts are created and authenticated separately. The first member performs a search, creating a search history record. The second member then attempts to delete the first member's search history entry by its ID. The test asserts that the API rejects the request with a permission denied error, and that the search history entry remains available for the original owner.

dependencies.purpose: Register two distinct member accounts to represent the owner and a non-owner.
Member 1 creates a search history entry that Member 2 is not allowed to delete.
Used to verify that the record remains for the owner after denied delete attempt.

scenarios.draft: A user with administrator privileges attempts to delete another user's search history record. After registering a member and admin accounts, and creating a search history entry as a member, the administrator successfully deletes this record using its ID. The test verifies deletion (API success and not-found on later fetch) and ensures compliance with admin override policies.

dependencies.purpose: Register both a standard member and a member eligible for administrative escalation.
Assign the administrator role to one of the members, enabling admin actions.
Create a search history entry as a normal member.
Used (a) to check record existence before deletion and (b) to assert not-found after admin deletion.

scenarios.draft: Test updating the action and action_reason fields of an existing moderation log entry by an authorized moderator. Create a member, escalate to moderator, create a log for a moderation event, then update action and action_reason (e.g., changing from 'hide' to 'delete' with a new reason). Ensure the record is correctly updated and changes reflected in the returned object. Verify all other immutable fields remain unchanged.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member account that will later be assigned moderator privileges.
Escalate member to moderator so they can perform moderation actions.
Create a moderation log entry for update testing. Must be created before the update scenario.

scenarios.draft: Test updating a moderation log with an invalid or non-existent log ID. Attempt to update an ID that does not exist in the database, and confirm that the system returns the appropriate not-found error, with no modification performed.

Test that unauthorized users (non-moderators/administrators) cannot update moderation logs. Attempt an update as a basic member or guest and confirm access is denied with an appropriate error response.

dependencies.purpose: Create a basic member account that does not have moderator privileges.
Create a moderation log entry for the test. Attempt update as a non-privileged actor.

scenarios.draft: Test successful hard-deletion of a moderation log entry by a user with administrator privileges. Create a member, escalate to administrator, create a moderation log, then perform a DELETE on the log record. Validate the log is no longer retrievable.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member account for admin role assignment.
Escalate member to administrator for delete authorization.
Create a moderation log record to be deleted.

scenarios.draft: Test that a user without administrator privileges cannot hard-delete a moderation log entry. Attempt deletion as a member or moderator (not administrator) and confirm a forbidden/unauthorized error is returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create a non-admin member account.
Create a moderation log entry to attempt unauthorized deletion.

scenarios.draft: Test deletion of a moderation log entry with a non-existent ID. Attempt to delete with a random or already-deleted UUID and verify system returns a not-found error, confirming no unintended side-effects.

Test successful creation of a warning issued by a moderator to a member. Create both a member and a moderator, then issue a warning from the moderator to the member with specified type and message. Verify the warning is correctly persisted and all required fields returned in the response.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member account to be warned.
Create a moderator to issue the warning.

scenarios.draft: Test creation of a warning with a non-existent member_id (warned user). Attempt to create warning with an invalid member UUID and verify system returns appropriate error without persisting the record.

dependencies.purpose: Create a moderator to issue the warning.

scenarios.draft: Test creation of two identical warnings (same member, moderator, type, message) and system handling. Verify that duplicate warnings are either allowed (and both recorded) or that idempotency/uniqueness is properly enforced per business rules with clear error responses.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member account to be warned.
Create a moderator who will issue repeated warnings.

scenarios.draft: Test listing warnings with various filtering parameters (by member_id, moderator_id, warning_type) and pagination. Create multiple warnings of varying types for different members and moderators. Perform list calls with filter/pagination in request and verify accuracy of returned records and total counts.

dependencies.purpose: Create member accounts to receive warnings.
Create moderator accounts to issue warnings.
Create multiple warning entries for various filter test conditions.

scenarios.draft: Test that soft-deleted warnings are not returned in standard warning lists. Create warnings, soft-delete one via DELETE endpoint, then list and verify the soft-deleted entry is not returned unless filters explicitly include soft-deleted records.

dependencies.purpose: Create member accounts for warning assignment.
Create moderators to issue warnings.
Create warnings for test. At least one will be soft-deleted.
Soft-delete a warning before listing to test exclusion logic.

scenarios.draft: Test fetching a warning detail by valid id as a moderator. Issue a warning, then retrieve it by its id and confirm all schema fields are present and correct.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member to be warned.
Create a moderator who issues the warning.
Create the warning for retrieval.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a warning with an invalid or soft-deleted id. Attempt fetch by random or deleted UUID and verify appropriate not-found or gone error, ensuring no sensitive data is leaked.

dependencies.purpose: First soft-delete a warning, then attempt to fetch to verify error behavior.

scenarios.draft: Test updating the actor_member_id of a mention notification. Start by creating a member who will be the original actor, and a second member who will be the new intended actor. Create a mention notification where the original member mentions another member. Update the mention using this endpoint to set actor_member_id to the new member's ID and validate that the change is correctly reflected. Then, attempt to update the mention to reference a non-existent actor_member_id (e.g., random UUID), and verify that the system rejects the request with a proper error indicating the referenced actor does not exist.

dependencies.purpose: Register members who will be used as both the original and updated actor for the mention event.
Create a mention notification associating an original actor_member_id and mentioned_member_id.

scenarios.draft: Test the hard deletion of a mention notification record. First, create two members and have one mention the other to generate a mention record. Then, use this endpoint to delete the mention by its id. After deletion, attempt to fetch the same mention by ID and verify that it returns a not found error, confirming irreversible removal. Additionally, test trying to delete a non-existent id to ensure a proper error response is returned.

dependencies.purpose: Register members to establish both an actor and target for the mention event.
Create a mention event between the two members to generate a mention notification.
Verify the mention has been deleted by attempting to fetch it after deletion.

scenarios.draft: Test creation of new vote types for the platform. Start by creating a vote type with a unique code and validate success. Next, attempt to create another vote type with the same code and verify that a unique constraint error is thrown. Confirm that only schema-defined fields are accepted and any extra fields are rejected. This covers both the happy path and uniqueness/business logic enforcement for voting type setup managed by administrators.

Test the retrieval of vote types with search and pagination criteria. First, create multiple vote type records (with varying codes and names) using the POST endpoint. Use this endpoint to search for a specific vote type by code and verify correct filtering. Then, retrieve the full list of vote types with pagination and confirm that the number of records per page and total count match expectations. Test searching with a mix of code, name, and sort options to cover business use cases of platform administration.

dependencies.purpose: Create multiple vote type records with varying attributes for effective search and pagination testing.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving vote type details using a valid and invalid id. First, create a vote type via the POST endpoint and fetch its ID. Then, use this GET endpoint to retrieve the vote type by its valid ID and verify that all fields match what was originally created. Next, attempt to fetch a vote type using a non-existent or malformed id and confirm that an appropriate not found error is returned, confirming robust business error handling.

dependencies.purpose: Create a vote type to generate a valid ID for subsequent retrieval.

scenarios.draft: Test a successful update to an administrator assignment, where the admin changes the assigned_at timestamp and sets the revoked_at timestamp (effectively revoking admin rights, e.g., for a role downgrade or compliance requirement). First, create a member account. Then, assign administrator rights to that member with the POST /discussionBoard/actors/administrators endpoint. Then, call this update endpoint using the created administrator assignment ID, setting a new revoked_at timestamp (to mark revocation) and observe that the administrator assignment now shows the correct revoked_at and possibly changed assigned_at. Ensure that only valid schema fields are accepted, and correct role-based authorization and audit trail are respected. Confirm that the action is rejected if performed by a non-privileged actor.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member account to escalate to administrator role.
Assign administrator role to the above member, generating the admin assignment that will be updated in this test.

scenarios.draft: Verify that attempting to update an administrator assignment using a non-existent or invalid ID returns a not found (404) error. Try to call this endpoint with a random UUID that does not correspond to an existing administrator assignment. Ensure that proper error handling and response format are enforced.

Test that if the request body for updating an administrator assignment contains fields not present in the schema (such as imaginary fields or audit metadata), the operation returns a validation error and does not perform any update. Confirm by preparing a valid update payload, adding an extra non-schema property, and verifying that a strict schema validation response is returned. Only code, member_id, assigned_at, and revoked_at are permitted.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member to promote to administrator and allow update attempt.
Assign admin role to the member, so that the test can attempt to update it with extra forbidden properties.

scenarios.draft: Test successful hard deletion of an administrator assignment. Create a member, assign administrator privileges, and then call this endpoint with the assignment ID. Verify that after successful deletion, any attempt to fetch this assignment returns not found (404), and that the administrator no longer appears in the admin assignment list.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member account that will be promoted to administrator.
Assign administrator role to the member, producing an assignment record that can be deleted.

scenarios.draft: Verify that attempting to delete a non-existent administrator assignment (with a random UUID or already deleted ID) results in a proper not found (404) response and no system changes. This ensures correct error semantics for accidental or malicious requests.

Test successful creation of a new top-level discussion thread by an authenticated member. Steps: Create a category (if required, to assign to thread), register a member, then use this endpoint to create a thread with all required schema fields (valid member ID as creator, valid category ID, title, and body content, as well as optional status flags like is_pinned and is_closed). Verify result includes all atomic fields and correct data is persisted. Confirm that only authenticated members can create threads and unauthorized actors are rejected.

dependencies.purpose: Create a category for use as the discussion_board_category_id on thread creation.
Register a member to be the thread creator.

scenarios.draft: Test creation of a thread with missing required fields (e.g., missing title or body, or missing creator member ID). Confirm that the system responds with a validation error, and thread is not created. This ensures schema-required fields are strictly enforced.

dependencies.purpose: Category is required to attempt at least a partially valid thread creation.
Member is required for member ID, allowing partial payloads to be tested for missing field behavior.

scenarios.draft: Test that creating a thread fails when supplied with a non-existent discussion_board_category_id or discussion_board_member_id (random UUIDs). Verify that a proper foreign key constraint or not-found error is returned and no thread is created. This tests the integrity of relations enforced by the system.

dependencies.purpose: Create at least one valid category for control, then use random/invalid IDs to test failure.
Create at least one valid member for control, but use random/invalid IDs to test error cases.

scenarios.draft: Verify that the threads list endpoint returns a paginated set of threads matching applied filters. Scenario: Create multiple threads by registering several members and assigning them to different categories, then request a filtered and paginated list (e.g., filter by category ID, status like is_pinned, or date range). Confirm the response contains only the threads matching filters, and pagination metadata is correct.

dependencies.purpose: Create several categories to assign to threads for filter testing.
Register members to author multiple threads.
Create threads with a variety of categories, authors, and statuses for test data.

scenarios.draft: Ensure that by default, threads with deleted_at set (soft deleted) do not appear in standard thread listing/search results. Scenario: Create several threads, perform a soft delete on one or more (via the DELETE endpoint), then request a list of threads without explicitly requesting deleted ones. Verify soft-deleted threads are excluded from normal results.

dependencies.purpose: Needed to create threads to be soft-deleted.
Members needed to create test threads.
Create multiple threads for control and deletion.
Perform soft-delete on at least one test thread to check exclusion logic.

scenarios.draft: Verify that a valid thread ID returns complete detail for that thread. Scenario: Create a category, a member, and a thread, and then fetch the thread using its ID. Ensure the returned object includes all schema-specified fields and matches the inserted data.

dependencies.purpose: Needed to create a thread.
Register a member to author the thread.
Create a new thread and obtain its ID for detailed fetch.

scenarios.draft: Ensure that requesting a thread by ID that is either non-existent or soft-deleted returns a not found (404) error or is otherwise hidden. Scenario: Attempt to get a thread using a random UUID (never created) and one that was previously soft-deleted via the DELETE endpoint. Confirm compliance with visibility and error handling requirements.

dependencies.purpose: Soft-delete a test thread to check exclusion from fetch by regular users.

scenarios.draft: Test successful creation of a configuration property by an administrator supplying a unique key, a value, and an optional description. Verify the response contains all schema fields, including audit timestamps, and the new configuration is available for immediate use.

Test that attempting to create a configuration property with a key that already exists results in a unique constraint error. First, create a configuration with a specific key. Then, attempt to create a second configuration with the same key and ensure the system rejects it and returns a unique constraint violation error.

dependencies.purpose: Create the first configuration property with a specific key to enable testing of uniqueness constraint for subsequent creation attempt.

scenarios.draft: Test that submitting additional, non-schema fields in the request body when creating a configuration property is rejected. The system should return a validation error, enforcing schema strictness.

Test that an administrator can list and search configuration properties with multiple filter criteria, pagination settings, and sort orders. Ensure the response contains only schema-defined fields for each item, adheres to pagination parameters, and respects all provided search criteria.

dependencies.purpose: Ensure at least one configuration property exists to appear in the list.

scenarios.draft: Test that searching for configuration properties using filters that do not match any records correctly returns an empty data array and accurate pagination meta.
Test that submitting a filter or sort parameter not present in the configuration schema causes the system to return a validation error, rejecting the request for referencing non-existent fields.

Test that retrieving a configuration property by its valid UUID returns all schema fields as expected, including key, value, description, and audit timestamps. The test must ensure the returned information matches what was stored during creation.

dependencies.purpose: Create a configuration property to obtain its UUID for the detail fetch test.

scenarios.draft: Test that attempting to fetch a configuration property with a non-existent or random UUID returns a 404 not found error.

Test that an administrator can update key, value, or description for a configuration property by its UUID, and the response reflects changes. The system must update the updated_at timestamp accordingly, and all returned fields must reflect the latest state as per schema.

dependencies.purpose: Create a configuration property to provide a UUID to update in this scenario.

scenarios.draft: Test that attempting to update the key of a configuration property to a value that already exists for another property results in a unique constraint error. Create two unique configurations, then try to set the second's key to the first's key and validate the error response.

dependencies.purpose: Create the first configuration with key A.
Create the second configuration with key B, which will be updated to key A to trigger the error.

scenarios.draft: Test that the system rejects updates that attempt to include non-schema fields in the request body when updating a configuration property. The response should indicate a validation error, enforcing schema field integrity.

dependencies.purpose: Create a configuration property to provide a UUID for update.

scenarios.draft: Test that an administrator can successfully hard delete a configuration property by its UUID, and the property is immediately and irreversibly removed from the system. Subsequent attempts to fetch the property must return a not found error. This validates both deletion functionality and system audit compliance for permanent deletes.

dependencies.purpose: Create a configuration property to obtain its UUID for deletion.

scenarios.draft: Test that attempting to delete a configuration property that does not exist (invalid UUID) results in a 404 not found error, and the system does not affect any existing records.

Verify that a guest session can be successfully created by supplying a unique session_token, valid ip_address, and optional user_agent. Ensure that the response includes all schema fields and correct timestamps. Validate business rule: session_token must be unique. The created session should be retrievable and can be used for guest-level activities. No soft delete applies. Dependencies: none.

Attempt to create a guest session with a session_token that already exists in the discussion_board_guests table. The first session is created successfully, and the second request with the same session_token should return a unique constraint violation error. This ensures system integrity by preventing duplicate guest sessions. Steps: create a valid guest session, then attempt another with the same session_token.

dependencies.purpose: Create the initial guest session with a specific session_token to setup the duplication scenario.

scenarios.draft: Test fetching an existing guest session by its UUID id. First, create a guest session and extract its id, then use GET to retrieve all of its details. Validate that returned data matches the guest record created and all necessary fields are included. This is used for audit or logging, and ensures guest records are stored and accessible.

dependencies.purpose: Set up a guest session record to retrieve using its id.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to fetch a guest session using an id that does not exist in the discussion_board_guests table. Verify that the API returns an appropriate 404 or not-found error response, demonstrating correct not-found handling for guest session audits, and that no sensitive data is leaked.

Verify that a new member account can be created using unique username and email, valid hashed_password, display_name, and (optionally) profile_image_url. The response should include all schema fields with correct audit/compliance timestamps, and set is_active appropriately. All uniqueness and format constraints must be tested. Created member is used for subsequent operations (GET, PATCH, PUT, DELETE).

Attempt to register a new member with a username that already exists. First, create a member with a unique username. Then, try to create a second member using the same username (with a different email). The system must return a uniqueness constraint error for username. This verifies system integrity and enforces the business rule for username uniqueness.

dependencies.purpose: Create an initial member with a unique username so that the next creation triggers the duplicate username scenario.

scenarios.draft: Test the system's handling of email uniqueness by creating one member with a unique email, then attempting to register a new member with the same email (with a different username). The operation should fail with a uniqueness violation for email, enforcing the business constraint.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member with a unique email to establish the conflict scenario for duplicate email registration.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to register a member using an invalid email format. Ensure that the API performs email format validation and returns an appropriate error for non-conforming email input. This ensures business data quality and protects downstream processes.

Test listing registered members using default filters and pagination. Create several members and use the PATCH endpoint to retrieve the list, verifying pagination structure, result correctness, and that soft-deleted or excluded members are not shown. Used for admin panels or member directories.

dependencies.purpose: Create one or more members to be listed during the member search operation.

scenarios.draft: Verify filtering capability by searching for members using a specific username that was registered previously. Ensure member search response returns only matching member records, with correct pagination and exclusion of soft-deleted or non-matching entries. Validates admin/delegated search workflows.

dependencies.purpose: Set up a member with a recognizable username for filter testing.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to filter members using search criteria (such as username or email) that does not match any record in the system. Validate that the response is a valid paginated structure with zero results, confirming correct handling of empty search results for admin or audit purposes.

Test retrieving a member's detail by id for a valid, existing member. First, use POST to create a member, then GET using its id. Ensure all member account (non-sensitive) fields are returned accurately and match what was stored during creation.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member and extract its id to be fetched using the GET endpoint.

scenarios.draft: Try to fetch a member that has already been soft-deleted by an administrator. After creating and deleting the member, attempt to GET using the member's id. The endpoint should return an error (such as 404), confirming that soft-deleted users are not exposed to detail queries, except for audit scenarios.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member whose record will then be deleted for the soft-delete error scenario.
Soft delete the member so that the subsequent GET returns an error.

scenarios.draft: Test successful update of a vote record by an administrator. First, create at least one vote type and a member account. Then, create a thread or post where a member casts an initial vote. Perform an update (as administrator) on an existing vote record using valid, schema-defined fields (such as changing vote_type, or updating the associated post_id, etc.). Validate that only allowed fields change and all business constraints (referential integrity, uniqueness per voter/content) are respected.

dependencies.purpose: Create a vote type needed for any valid vote operation.
Register a member who can create votes.
Create a thread to serve as the target of voting, using the registered member as creator.
Create an initial vote record to later update.

scenarios.draft: Test updating a non-existent vote record. Attempt to update a vote by using a UUID that does not exist in the discussion_board_votes table. Confirm that the system returns a not found (404) error and does not perform any data mutation.

Test update rejection when request body includes fields that are not part of the vote schema. Try to update a vote record with invalid or extra fields in the request payload. System should ignore or reject non-schema fields and provide a clear error response.

dependencies.purpose: Create a vote type for setup.
Register a member and create a valid initial vote record.
Create a thread for the initial vote.
Create the target vote record to attempt updating.

scenarios.draft: Test permanent deletion of a vote record by a moderator. First, create necessary entities (vote type, member, thread or post, and a vote). As a moderator, delete the vote record using a valid vote ID. Confirm that the record is irreversibly removed and cannot be retrieved by GET operations nor considered in subsequent voting or counts.

dependencies.purpose: Create a vote type for voting.
Register a member and create a thread or post for voting.
Create target thread.
Create vote record which will be deleted.

scenarios.draft: Test deletion attempt of a non-existent vote (invalid or previously-deleted ID). Try to delete a vote record using a UUID not present in the system. Verify a suitable not found (404) error is returned and data integrity remains unaffected.

Test creation of a new discussion board tag by an administrator. Provide a unique name and, optionally, a description. Verify the tag appears in the system, and all returned properties are per schema. Confirm that system-managed fields (created_at, updated_at, deleted_at) are managed by the server and returned in the response.

Test prevention of duplicate tag creation. Create a tag with a particular name, then attempt to create another with the same name. Expect a unique constraint error and verify system does not create the duplicate.

dependencies.purpose: Initial creation of a tag to establish uniqueness constraint.

scenarios.draft: Test rejection of extra or non-schema fields on tag creation. Attempt to submit a tag creation request including fields not defined in the schema. System should reject the request with an error indicating invalid input.

Test tag list retrieval with keyword searching and pagination. Create several tags, then perform a PATCH request with filters on name or description and specific pagination settings. Validate that filters and paging metadata operate properly and only schema-defined tags are returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create one or more tags to populate the list for searching/filtering.

scenarios.draft: Test listing tags including soft-deleted records when the request filters explicitly allow deleted tags. First, create and then soft-delete a tag. Then perform a search specifying inclusion of deleted_at records. Ensure that the soft-deleted tag is returned in the result, with proper deleted_at metadata present.

dependencies.purpose: Create a tag to subsequently delete.
Soft delete a created tag for retrieval as a soft-deleted record.

scenarios.draft: Test error response when using invalid fields in search request. Attempt to use non-schema fields in tag search/filter parameters. Verify that the system rejects the request with a validation error and does not return results.
Test retrieval of tag record by its valid UUID. First, create a tag. Then, fetch the tag using its id. Ensure the full schema-defined object is returned with all necessary fields.

dependencies.purpose: Create a tag to be retrieved by ID.

scenarios.draft: Test behavior when requesting a tag with an invalid or non-existent UUID. Attempt to fetch a tag by a UUID not present in the system, and verify that a not found (404) or similar error is returned.

Test access to a tag that has been soft deleted. First, create and then soft-delete a tag. Attempt to retrieve the tag by id and ensure that the correct error or exclusion policy is enforced (e.g., not found or record marked as deleted).

dependencies.purpose: Create a tag for eventual soft deletion.
Soft-delete the tag before trying to retrieve it.

scenarios.draft: Test successful creation of a new channel by an administrator supplying a unique code, name, and optional description. Confirm the returned channel contains expected fields (code, name, description, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at is null), and that it is available for immediate use in the system. No extra fields should be accepted or returned.

Attempt to create a channel with a code that already exists in the database. First, an administrator creates a channel with a unique code. Then, a second create attempt is made with the same code but different name/description. Verify that the API returns a unique constraint error for code. These steps must be performed in sequence to establish the conflict.

dependencies.purpose: A valid channel must be created first to have a duplicate code in the system.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to create a channel with extra fields not defined in the schema (e.g., attempting to set deleted_at or an unrelated field). Verify that the system ignores or rejects the request as per schema enforcement, returning an appropriate validation error or ignoring extra fields in the response.
Attempt to create a channel omitting required fields such as code or name. Verify the API returns a clear validation error indicating missing required fields and does not create the channel.

Test searching for channels by keyword in code or name with pagination. Create several channels first, then search using partial matches and pagination parameters. Verify the response includes only channels matching the criteria, with correct pagination metadata, and each channel object matches schema fields.

dependencies.purpose: Create multiple channels with varying names and codes to populate search space.

scenarios.draft: Test searching for channels including both active and soft-deleted entries. First, create multiple channels and then soft-delete one of them. Execute a search request specifying inclusion of soft-deleted channels. Confirm that both active and soft-deleted channels are listed in the response, and deleted_at is set on deleted ones.

dependencies.purpose: Create multiple channels so one can be soft-deleted.
Soft-delete one channel by setting deleted_at for testing inclusion in results.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to search for channels using a filter field that does not exist in the schema. Verify the API returns a validation error indicating that the filter is invalid.
Test retrieving a channel's detailed information by valid id. First, create a channel, then fetch it by its id and verify all expected schema fields are returned with accurate data.

dependencies.purpose: A channel must exist (created) to fetch its details by id.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to fetch a channel using a non-existent or invalid id. Verify that the API returns a not-found error and does not expose any sensitive or unrelated error data.

Test admin access policy by fetching a channel that has been soft-deleted (deleted_at set). First, create and then soft-delete a channel, then attempt to fetch its details by id. Verify policy-compliant behavior—either returned with deleted_at set, or returns appropriate error if soft-deleted channels are excluded from detail view.

dependencies.purpose: Create a channel that will later be soft-deleted.
Soft-delete the created channel for test purpose.

scenarios.draft: Test updating the name and description of a channel using its id. Create a channel, then update name and description, and verify that only those fields—and updated_at—are changed in the returned object, with code and other fields remaining unchanged.

dependencies.purpose: Create a channel to provide a valid id for update flow.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to update a channel's code to a value that is already in use by another channel. Create two channels with different codes, then attempt to update the second channel to use the first's code. Verify the API returns a unique constraint violation error.

dependencies.purpose: Create two channels to test code uniqueness on update.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to update a channel using fields not present in the schema (e.g., deleted_at). Confirm that update is ignored for unsupported fields or causes a validation error according to system policy.

dependencies.purpose: Ensure there is a channel to attempt invalid update on.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to update a channel using an invalid or non-existent id. Verify that the API returns a not-found error and does not update any resource.
Test successfully soft-deleting a channel by updating its deleted_at field. Create a channel, then perform a soft delete using its id and verify the returned object has deleted_at set.

dependencies.purpose: Create a channel to soft-delete for the test.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to soft-delete a channel using a non-existent id. Verify the API returns a clear not-found error and does not affect any other channel records.

Test updating both the target_type and target_id fields of a subscription record. The test should first create a member and a new subscription for that member to a thread, then update the subscription to follow a different resource (e.g., change from following a thread to following a category or tag). The system should allow this, reflect the updated values, and maintain schema integrity.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member account required for subscription ownership.
Create an initial subscription record for the member to update.

scenarios.draft: Test failure when attempting to update a subscription's target_type to a value not accepted by the schema (e.g., a non-existent type). First, create a member and a valid subscription, then attempt to update with an invalid target_type. The API should reject the update and return a schema validation error.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member to own the subscription.
Create a valid subscription for the member to update.

scenarios.draft: Test permission denial when a user attempts to update a subscription they do not own. Set up two members: create a subscription under the first, then have the second member attempt to update it. Expect a 404 or permission-denied response, ensuring ownership is enforced.

dependencies.purpose: Create the first member who will own the subscription.
Create a second member who will attempt unauthorized update.
Create a subscription assigned to the first member.

scenarios.draft: Test successful deletion of a notification subscription by its owner (member). The scenario requires creating a member, then a subscription for that member, followed by deleting it. Verify the deletion is permanent by confirming subsequent GET on the same id returns 404.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member account to own the subscription.
Create a subscription under this member.

scenarios.draft: Test refusal of hard delete when a non-owner member attempts to remove a subscription they do not own. Two members are set up: one creates the subscription, the other attempts deletion. Expect a 404 or permission-denied response to validate authorization logic.

dependencies.purpose: Create the first member to own the subscription.
Create a second member who attempts the unauthorized deletion.
Create the subscription resource to be targeted for deletion.

scenarios.draft: Test that attempting to delete a subscription record that does not exist or has already been deleted returns a 404 error. The test attempts to delete using a random or previously deleted UUID.

Test successful creation of a mention event where a member mentions another member in a post. Create two member accounts, a post authored by the first member, then simulate a mention event targeting the second member. Verify the created mention points to the correct actor, mentioned member, and post context.

Create the member to be mentioned.

scenarios.draft: Test failure when attempting to create a mention event with an invalid content_id (e.g., referencing a post or thread that doesn't exist). Set up two members, then attempt to create a mention with a fake UUID as content_id. Expect an error indicating invalid foreign key reference.

Mentioned member receiving the mention.

scenarios.draft: Test listing mention events for a given member with pagination support. Create two members and at least two distinct mentions targeting the same member in different content contexts (e.g., one for a post, one for a comment). List mentions for the mentioned member, using pagination parameters to retrieve results in multiple pages, verifying correct counts and content.

dependencies.purpose: Actor member needed for mentions.
Mentioned member.
Create a thread for post context.
Create a post for mention context.
Create a comment as a different mention context.
Mention for post.
Mention for comment.

scenarios.draft: Test mention listing with actor_member_id and mentioned_member_id filters. Create three members, generate mentions initiated by each member, some mentioning themselves and some mentioning others. Use the API to filter mention events by both actor_member_id and mentioned_member_id, verifying filtering logic returns only intended results.

dependencies.purpose: First member to act as both actor and mentioned in different tests.
Second member.
Third member.
Mention scenario 1.
Mention scenario 2.
Mention scenario 3.

scenarios.draft: Test successfully fetching the complete detail of a mention by its ID. The scenario should begin by creating an actor member, a mentioned member, and a content entity (e.g., post or comment), then create a mention event. Fetch the mention by its ID and verify all fields are correct.

dependencies.purpose: Actor member to initiate a mention.
Mentioned member to receive a mention.
Thread to provide content context.
Post for the mention's content context.
Create the actual mention event to fetch by ID.

scenarios.draft: Test that fetching a mention notification with a non-existent or invalid ID returns a not-found error. The scenario simply attempts a GET with a random UUID never used for mention creation, confirming the response is a 404.

Test updating the name and description of a tag with valid new data. Begin by creating an administrator account and a tag with an initial name and description. Then, perform an update to change the tag's name to a unique valid value and update the description. Verify that the returned tag object reflects the new name and description, and the updated_at timestamp has advanced.

dependencies.purpose: Create an initial tag to update. Required to obtain tag id for the update operation.

scenarios.draft: Test updating a tag's name to a value already used by another tag, which should return a uniqueness constraint error. Start with two distinct tags created by an administrator. Attempt to update one tag's name to the name of the other tag. Verify that the system responds with an appropriate duplicate name error and does not allow the update.

dependencies.purpose: Create two distinct tags with different names for setup. Use one as the source, one as the duplicate target.

scenarios.draft: Test updating a tag that does not exist. Attempt to update a tag using a random or deleted tag id. Verify that the response is a 404 Not Found error and no tag is changed in the system.

Test updating a tag that has been soft-deleted. Create a tag and then soft-delete it using the DELETE endpoint. Attempt to update the name or description of the soft-deleted tag. Verify that the system rejects the update with an error, referencing that the tag is deleted or inaccessible.

dependencies.purpose: Create a tag to test soft-delete condition.
Soft-delete the tag before attempting the update, to simulate updating a deleted tag.

scenarios.draft: Test updating a tag using a request body containing fields not supported by the schema, such as id or created_at, or completely unrelated fields. Verify that the API rejects the request with a validation error and does not perform any update or change to the tag.

dependencies.purpose: Create a tag to test invalid update payloads.

scenarios.draft: Test successful soft deletion of a tag. Create a tag as an administrator, then soft delete it by calling the DELETE endpoint. Verify that the returned object shows 'deleted_at' is set and that the tag is no longer available in normal tag listings or for assignment to posts/threads.

dependencies.purpose: Create a tag to soft delete.

scenarios.draft: Test attempting to soft delete a tag with a non-existent or random id. Verify that the system returns an appropriate error (404 Not Found) and no tag is affected.

Test soft-deleting a tag that has already been soft-deleted. Create a tag and soft delete it. Attempt to soft-delete the same id again. Verify that the system rejects the second deletion and returns an already deleted or not found error.

dependencies.purpose: Create a tag to be soft-deleted twice in sequence.
First soft-deletion to mark tag as deleted.

scenarios.draft: Test successful creation of a new category with a unique name and optional description by an administrator. Verify that the returned resource has the correct name, description, and system-managed fields like created_at and updated_at are properly set.

Test creating a new category with a name that is already used by another category. Start by creating an initial category, then attempt a second category creation with the same name. System should reject the second request with a unique constraint error.

dependencies.purpose: Create the initial category with a given name for uniqueness conflict setup.

scenarios.draft: Test creating a category with missing required fields (specifically omitting the 'name'). System should return a validation error indicating the required field is missing.
Test creating a category with extra fields not supported by the schema (such as id, timestamps, or random fields). API should reject the request with a validation error and not create a category.

Test listing categories with typical pagination and filtering. Create 5+ categories with distinct names and descriptions. List categories, filtering by a substring of the name and specify a page size less than total records to test pagination. Verify returned results match the filter, are paginated, and total count is correct.

dependencies.purpose: Create multiple (at least 5) categories for testing pagination and filtering.

scenarios.draft: Test listing categories including soft-deleted entities. Create several categories, soft-delete at least one, then list categories using request parameters that include soft-deleted records. Verify that the deleted category appears in the result set with deleted_at properly set.

dependencies.purpose: Create several categories, some of which will be soft-deleted.
Soft delete a category to make it available for deleted record testing.

scenarios.draft: Test searching for categories by partial match on the description field. Create categories with unique descriptions. Perform a search using a partial description keyword and verify that only categories whose descriptions contain the keyword are returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create categories with unique descriptions to enable search by description.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving the details of a single category by its id. Create a new category, then fetch it by id. Verify that all fields are correctly returned and match those set during creation/computed by the system.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new category to obtain a valid id for retrieval.

scenarios.draft: Test fetching the details of a category with a non-existent id. Attempt to retrieve a category using a random or deleted id and verify that the system returns a 404 Not Found or equivalent error response.

Test that fetching a soft-deleted category by id returns appropriate error or gone status. Create a category, soft delete it, then attempt to retrieve it by id. Verify proper error response is returned for deleted resources.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new category for soft-delete testing.
Soft delete category before attempting retrieval.

scenarios.draft: Test successful update of a moderation report by assigning a moderator, changing its status to 'in_progress,' and adding resolution notes. First, create and submit a moderation report with required fields. Next, update the report by assigning the moderator's ID to the 'moderator_id' field, set status to 'in_progress', and include an initial resolution note. Validate that the returned report reflects these updates (moderator assigned, status changed, and notes present).

Create the report to obtain the report ID for updating.
Create a new member who will be escalated to moderator.
Escalate the new member to moderator, whose ID will be assigned to the report update.

scenarios.draft: Test updating a report's status to 'resolved' and providing 'resolution_notes' and 'resolved_at'. Create a member and moderator, register a content report, and then update the report by setting status to 'resolved', specifying resolution notes, and setting the current timestamp for 'resolved_at'. Confirm the report is properly updated in all respective fields, and audit trails reflect the resolution. Attempt to update immutable fields, such as 'reporter_member_id', and ensure an appropriate error is returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member account to use as the report's reporter.
Create a post to report.
Create the report to obtain report ID for update.
Create and escalate a member to moderator for report assignment.
Assign moderator, whose ID will be used in the update.

scenarios.draft: Test invalid update scenarios for a moderation report: attempt to update forbidden fields ('reporter_member_id', 'created_at', or 'deleted_at') or use a report ID that doesn't exist. dependencies.purpose: Create a member to file a report.
Create the content to be reported.
Create the report to obtain the report ID for the invalid update.

scenarios.draft: Test that a moderation report can be soft deleted by a moderator and that after deletion, the report appears with 'deleted_at' set and is omitted from normal report listings. Begin by creating a member, content (thread, post, or comment), reporting the content, and then soft deleting the report by ID as a moderator. Afterwards, attempt to list or fetch the report and verify it's either omitted or appropriately flagged as deleted. Audit the 'deleted_at' field is set.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member to submit a report.
Create a thread for report targeting.
File the moderation report.

scenarios.draft: Test that attempting to soft delete a moderation report that does not exist or has already been soft deleted returns an error (404 or 409 depending on implementation). Attempt to delete a random/non-existing ID and also delete the same report twice in succession. Confirm both cases yield appropriate error responses.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member for valid report submission.
Create a thread that is the content target of the report.
Create a report to first delete and then duplicate-delete.

scenarios.draft: Test successful creation of a moderation log for a content moderation action on a thread. Create a moderator, a thread, then record a moderation action (e.g., 'delete' or 'hide') on the thread with 'action_reason' specified. Validate the returned moderation log contains correct moderator, target thread, action, and reason, and that timestamps are present and reflect recent action.

dependencies.purpose: Create member account to elevate to moderator.
Escalate member to moderator.
Create a thread so a moderation action can be performed.

scenarios.draft: Test that attempts to create a moderation log with invalid or non-existent thread_id, post_id, or comment_id references return an appropriate error (400/404). This prevents logging moderation actions against missing targets. Try to create logs for content IDs that were never created and confirm the errors.

Create the moderator record; then use invalid IDs for content references.

scenarios.draft: Test full search and filter capabilities of moderation logs: create multiple moderators and various actions on different threads/posts/comments, then filter logs by moderator_id, action, and target content reference. Validate paginated results only contain matching logs and correct meta (total count, pagination info).

dependencies.purpose: Create two members and escalate both to moderators.
Escalate first member to moderator.
Escalate second member to moderator.
Create several threads for moderation logs.
Log various moderation actions tied to moderators and content to later filter on.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a single moderation log by its ID. Confirm that a valid ID returns the log's full details (moderator, content, action, reason, and timestamp). dependencies.purpose: Create member who will become moderator.
Elevate member to moderator.
Create content for the moderation action.

scenarios.draft: Test updating both the name and description of an existing category. Scenario: As an administrator, create a category first (to obtain a valid category id), then send a PUT request to update the 'name' and 'description' fields with new valid values. This test validates the primary use case for category updates and ensures system persistence and correct field mapping.

scenarios.draft: Test attempting to update a category to a name that already exists for a different category. Create two categories first, then try to update the second category's name field to that of the first category. Confirm that the category does not appear in standard list results after deletion.

dependencies.purpose: Create a category to generate a valid id for the soft delete scenario.
Query list of categories before and after soft deletion to check disappearance from normal listings.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to soft delete a category using a random/non-existent uuid. The API must return a 404 Not Found or an appropriate error response. The test ensures non-existent/deleted records cannot be soft deleted again.

Soft delete a category twice in succession. First, create a category and soft delete it. Then, attempt to soft delete it again. The API should respond with an error indicating the category has already been deleted or is not found. This checks idempotency and correct error handling for already soft-deleted entities.

dependencies.purpose: Create a category for initial soft deletion and repeat deletion attempt.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to fetch a search history record belonging to another user as a different (non-privileged) member. The endpoint should reject access with an unauthorized error (403), ensuring compliance with privacy and data protection rules.

dependencies.purpose: Register member A (author of the post).
